statement: Show that there is a set of \(2002\) distinct positive integers such that the sum of one or more elements of the set is never a perfect square, cube, or higher power.

\(ABCD\) is a cyclic quadrilateral and \(M\) is a point on side \(CD\) such that triangle \(ADM\) and quadrilateral \(ABCM\) have the same area and the same perimeter. Show that two sides of \(ABCD\) have equal length.

The squares of an \(m \times n\) board are labeled from \(1\) to \(mn\) so that squares labeled \(i\) and \(i+1\) always share a side. Show that for some \(k\), the squares labeled \(k\) and \(k+3\) also share a side.

For any non-empty subset \(A\) of \(\{1, 2, \ldots, n\}\), define \(f(A)\) as the largest element of \(A\) minus the smallest element of \(A\). Find \(\sum f(A)\) where the sum is taken over all non-empty subsets of \(\{1, 2, \ldots, n\}\).
A finite collection of squares has total area \(4\). Show that they can be arranged to cover a unit square (a square of side \(1\)).
Show that one cannot form more than \(4096\) binary sequences of length \(24\) such that any two sequences differ in at least \(8\) positions.
